newsitem.title: USA: Glaxo Wellcome, IGI in dermatology pact.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo Wellcome, IGI in dermatology pact.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Inc and IGI Inc said on Wednesday Glaxo would assume responsibility for sales and marketing of IGI's domestic line of dermatology products at the end of the month.
The products will be marketed by Glaxo Dermatology, a division of Glaxo Wellcome Inc, it said.
Under the agreement, IGI said it would manufacture a line of skin care products using the patented Novasome lipid vesicle microencapsulation technology for Glaxo.
Novosome is a patented skin care delivery system which provides glycolic acid formulations.

As part of the deal, IGI said it granted Glaxo exclusive rights to the Novasome trademark, in connection with the sale of the product line to dermatologists and other licensed professionals operating in the United States.
Glaxo Wellcome said it would pay IGI certain upfront amounts, product manufacturing costs and royalty payments and other incentives on future sales of the product line.
IGI and Glaxo Wellcome said they would work together to develop new products based on the Novasome technology.

IGI said it would retain its rights to sell its skin care products abroad and to other market segments in the United States. IGI would continue to develop new skin care products based on the patented Novasome technology.
Edward Hager, chairman and CEO of IGI, said: "This agreement with Glaxo is expected to make a valuable contribution to our operating results in 1997."
